title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
summary:
Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th.
As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen.
The move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 percent AI-generated.
“We believe this will resonate with both artists and listeners alike, as 96% of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays at all,” Andersen adds.
The platform is also going to ban music distributors from submitting AI songs, using the AI detection tool Ircam Amplify and metadata checks to reject submissions generated solely with AI.

title: US approves SpaceX plan to send a million data satellites to space
summary:

title: What Australia’s ‘Digital Duty of Care’ Law Means for Big Tech
summary:
Under the Digital Duty of Care law, platforms must provide risk assessments to regulators at least once a year, and they must notify regulators before they introduce significant changes to their platforms that could allow for new risks of harm, such as “addictive” design features.
The amendments also make it easier for Australian citizens to hold tech companies to account.
Previously, one needed to rely on complex legal avenues concerning company negligence and consumer protection.
The new law grants Australians the “private right of action,” which means they can directly sue digital platforms for breaching their duty of care.
